run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:08:54Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by frontend-proxy's own server-side ingress spans: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} turns nonzero at 13:45:54Z and its 5-minute rate equals exactly 0.011111111111111112 at 14:09:54Z and 14:10:54Z, matching the alert annotation's 0.01111111111111111; because the condition is an error rate above 0, a handful of errors per hour keeps it firing. The error spans are not abstract: the frontend-proxy access log shows them as HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} against upstream cluster frontend (Service frontend, ClusterIP 100.71.53.109:8080), and each of the 10 readable 503 lines lines up with one increment of the error counter. Volume is tiny (~20 error spans in the hour versus 24,771 UNSET ingress spans, about 0.08%), the failures are ordinary GETs on four different frontend routes, no pod in the namespace restarted, no node is under pressure, and the only change event in the window is a controller-driven load-generator rollout at 13:59:44-45Z that postdates the first errors. The deepest supported conclusion is therefore that the frontend upstream terminated pooled connections before response headers and Envoy converted that into 503s; why the frontend side terminated them could not be established because the frontend container produced no readable logs, frontend spans carry no status code, and Jaeger holds no trace after 13:42:12Z.

claims.text: The alert's value matches frontend-proxy's ingress error-span rate exactly: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} with a 5-minute rate equals 0.011111111111111112 at 14:09:54Z and 14:10:54Z, is first nonzero at 13:45:54Z (0.003703703703703704/s) and peaks at 0.02592592592592593/s at 13:51:54Z.

Only the ingress operation of frontend-proxy carries error status: over 55 minutes traces_span_metrics_calls_total increased by 20.294117647058826 spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 24771.0 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET for span_name "ingress", while span_name "router frontend egress" increased 0 with STATUS_CODE_ERROR; a 1-hour increase gives the same 20.294117647058826 error spans.

The frontend-proxy access log records the errors as HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}: 10 such lines between 13:58:43.653716Z and 14:12:33.650553Z, each with 0 bytes received, 95 bytes sent and durations of 140, 208, 222, 242, 342, 452, 602, 604, 673 and 687 ms, all on upstream cluster frontend (upstream host 100.71.53.109:8080) for GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, /api/products/66VCHSJNUP, /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM, /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z, /api/recommendations?productIds=2ZYFJ3GM2N, /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars, /api/data/?contextKeys=travel, /api/data/?contextKeys=books and /api/cart.

Each logged 503 corresponds to an error-span increment: the cumulative error counter was 434 at 13:58:44Z, 435 at 13:59:44Z, 436 at 14:01:44Z, 438 at 14:02:44Z, 439 at 14:04:44Z, 441 at 14:08:44Z, 442 at 14:09:44Z, 443 at 14:11:44Z and 444 at 14:13:44Z, matching the 10 access-log 503 timestamps (13:58:43, 14:00:46, two at 14:01:29, 14:03:35, 14:06:58, 14:07:15, 14:08:28, 14:10:20, 14:12:33), and the counter then stayed at 444 through 14:18:44Z.

The failed upstream is the frontend Service: otel-demo Service frontend has ClusterIP 100.71.53.109 on port 8080, the upstream host printed on every 503 line, and the backing pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 (podIP 100.96.2.93, node 10.0.129.6, the same node as frontend-proxy pod 100.96.2.11) is Running and Ready with restartCount 0.

The error spans last longer than normal ingress traffic, consistent with requests that were in flight and then terminated rather than immediate local rejections: of the 20.294117647058826 error spans, 0 were <=100 ms, 2 were in (100,200] ms, 7.1 in (200,400] ms and 11.2 in (400,800] ms, whereas among the 24771 UNSET ingress spans 58.8% were <=10 ms and 80.3% <=100 ms.

The cumulative error counter was already 424 at the first returned sample (13:39:44Z) and stayed 424 through 13:44:44Z, so 424 ingress error spans were counted between the otel-collector container start at 13:27:57Z and 13:39:44Z and lie outside every rate window the alert evaluates; only the later 20 errors (13:45:44Z onward) are the ongoing sporadic failures.

In a sampled window without errors the proxy returned almost only success codes: for 14:11:44Z-14:11:57Z the log held 133 lines matching 'HTTP/1.1" 200' out of 1287 lines read (only 18 in-window lines failed to match that pattern, which includes 308 redirects and any failures), so failures are a tiny minority of requests in that sample rather than a broad 4xx/5xx pattern.

Pod and node state contradict a crash, eviction or capacity cause: all 21 otel-demo Deployments report 1 desired / 1 available / 1 ready / 1 updated, every listed pod container is Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, the only events in the window are the load-generator rollout (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, SuccessfulDelete, Killing at 13:59:44-45Z), and all 5 nodes are Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

CPU throttling does not track the 503s: frontend-proxy was throttled in 1127.7777777777776 of 20348.33333333333 CFS periods over 55 minutes (about 5.5%), continuously every minute (12.6-41.2 throttled periods per minute from 13:40:44Z to 14:13:44Z), and that ratio is lower than frontend (27.5%), cart (23.3%), postgresql (23.3%) and product-catalog (19.1%), so throttling is not a frontend-proxy-specific trigger for these sparse errors.

The load-generator rollout at 13:59:44-45Z did not cause the alert: the error counter was already rising at 13:45:44Z (424 to 425) and reached 435 before the rollout minute, the rollout was the Deployment's own controller replacing pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 with load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb (SuccessfulDelete/Killing then SuccessfulCreate/Started, new pod with 0 restarts), and the load-generator env is a normal headless test (LOCUST_USERS=50, LOCUST_HOST=http://frontend-proxy:8080).

The 503s arise because the frontend side of the pooled HTTP connection closes it before response headers (Envoy detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}), e.g. an HTTP keepalive/idle-connection race between Envoy's upstream pool and the frontend HTTP server, or a reset on the ClusterIP path (both pods sit on node 10.0.129.6); since the 10 sampled failures are ordinary GETs to four different routes, no single frontend endpoint is broken.

The alert is sensitive by design rather than indicating a broad outage: it fires on an error rate above 0 while sustained failure volume is 20.294117647058826 error spans out of 24791.294117647058 total ingress spans over 55 minutes (about 0.08%), so a few terminated connections per hour keep the condition true.

frontend-proxy's own outbound handling is not the failing leg: its "router frontend egress" spans never carry error status (increase 0 over 55 minutes) and the 503 responses are Envoy's standard 95-byte local replies, so the proxy relayed a connection failure rather than a 5xx response body; the frontend's own spans carry no status code at all (every frontend operation reports STATUS_CODE_UNSET and its error series stay flat at 0), so a frontend application failure can be neither confirmed nor excluded from span metrics.

Align the keepalive/timeout settings between the frontend HTTP server and the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster (idle timeout and keepalive probing) and consider retry_on_reset for idempotent GETs, then re-check whether upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} disappears from the proxy access log.

Inspect node 10.0.129.6 (where frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth both run) for conntrack/nftables drops at the 503 timestamps, and make the frontend container actually emit logs, since neither its stdout nor its spans currently expose request failures.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule so a single error span does not page: the observed sustained rate is about 0.08% of ingress spans, so an error-ratio threshold (or a longer for-duration / minimum error count) would match the real impact better than 'above 0'.

gaps: Frontend application logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs on frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 for 14:00:00Z-14:13:40Z returned no_data after reading 0 bytes and 0 lines, so the frontend-side reason for terminating the connections cannot be read.

Jaeger holds no trace after 13:42:12Z: traces_search for frontend-proxy over 14:13:44Z-14:18:44Z returned no_data (0 traces) and the earlier sampled span view's data_as_of was 13:42:12.175666Z, so the 503 requests logged from 13:58:43Z onward cannot be inspected as traces and their span tags are unknown.

Trace searches for frontend-proxy with tag error=true, http.status_code=503 and http.status_code=500 all returned no_data (no matching trace), so trace-tag evidence for the failed requests does not exist in this Run; the 503 status is established only from the proxy access log.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total carries no HTTP status-code label, so the status behind each ERROR ingress span is only known for the 10 access-log lines that were readable, not for the 424 earlier errors.

frontend-proxy's readable log retention in this Run starts at 13:56:45Z, so errors between 13:45:44Z and 13:56:45Z and the 424 pre-13:39:44Z errors have no log evidence, and a scan of 13:56:45Z-13:56:56Z and 14:01:44Z-14:02:44Z for non-200/308 statuses returned no_data rather than a confirmed zero.

The alert rule definition is not available: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for all alerting rules, so the exact expression and threshold other than the annotation's 'above 0' are unknown.

The change_history integration is not available, so the cause of the 13:27:54-13:29:39Z namespace-wide ReplicaSet creation (including the flagd ReplicaSet replacement at 13:29:37Z) and of the 13:59:44Z load-generator rollout cannot be verified.

kube_pod_container_info returned no_data for this namespace, so image digests could not be compared to tell whether the rollouts were config-only; the otel-collector log query for 13:30:00Z-14:18:44Z also returned no_data (0 lines read), so collector-side errors are unverified.
Node-level conntrack or packet-drop telemetry was not available in this Run, so a network-path cause for connection_termination remains untested.
next_steps: Compare the frontend Node/Next.js keepAliveTimeout and headersTimeout with the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster idle_timeout/keepalive settings, and test a retry_on_reset policy for GET requests.
Inspect node 10.0.129.6 for conntrack table exhaustion or nftables/kube-proxy connection drops around 13:58:43Z-14:12:33Z.
Check whether the frontend process logs anywhere other than container stdout and whether it records aborted requests or crashed route handlers.
Re-evaluate the RequestErrorRate rule against an error-ratio threshold rather than a rate above 0.
